title: Invocation swimlane cost sculptor: interactive per-route token attribution & export
creator: Priya Nair
description: Create an interactive "swimlane" visualization in Redwood Console that lets engineers and platform owners explore invocation-level token usage and attribute cost across routes, model variants, and rollout cohorts. The 'cost sculptor' should enable brush selection across time and session axes, reveal per-invocation token breakdowns (prompt/response/system), surface inferred cost drivers (batching, kv-cache hits, quantization variant), and let users export selected rows as CSV/JSON and snapshot a shareable link. Primary goals: quickly identify token-cost hotspots, support chargeback exports, and help PMs/designers validate rollout cost regressions during canary/A-B testing.
acceptance_criteria: Design prototype in Figma with at least two density modes: compact (high row count) and expanded (detailed tokens + timeline)
Users can filter lanes by route, model, region, and rollout tag and apply brush selection over time ranges
Hover/selection details include: total tokens, prompt tokens, response tokens, estimated cost (USD), avg latency, batching indicator, kv-cache hit rate
Export button generates CSV with selected rows and fields (invocation_id, timestamp, route, model, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, estimated_cost_usd, rollout_tag)
Role-aware UI: engineers see raw invocation IDs and debug links; finance sees anonymized user/tenant names and export presets
Prototype demonstrates mobile-responsiveness for vertical space-constrained consoles and accessibility semantics for screen readers
Design handoff artifacts include measurements, color tokens, animation spec for brush, and edge-case states (no data, sampled view, truncated rows)
Engineering feasibility signoff from ENG owners (see dependencies) documented in comments
design_notes: Swimlane rows represent aggregation buckets by route + model variant by default; users can 'expand' a bucket to inspect raw invocations
Use color saturation to indicate cost-per-invocation (not absolute tokens) to avoid misinterpretation when latency spikes create long responses
Micro-interaction: brush selection should snap to invocation boundaries but allow fractional selection for long-running streams
Include a small sparklines column for per-row token rate to help detect sudden spikes without expanding the row
Provide an 'explain' pill that surfaces the heuristic used to convert tokens -> estimated cost (model rate table, quantization multiplier, batching factor)
When sampling is applied due to volume limits, show a clear banner and provide a 'request full export' CTA that ties into Dedicated quota flow
tradeoffs: High-density view vs. actionable detail: default to aggregated rows to maintain performance, with a progressive disclosure pattern for deeper inspection
Live streaming of invocations could produce jitter; prefer 5s poll or websocket with debounce to keep brush stable
Accurate cost requires correlating with historical batching and kernel selection data that lives in ENG runtime; initial version will show an estimated cost using recent averages
Role-aware anonymization adds complexity to exports; implement simple mapping rules first, maintain audit logs for later compliance requirements
decisions: Adopt 'swimlane + brush' as the primary interaction rather than a heatmap to preserve per-invocation identifiers
Export format chosen: CSV for finance and JSON for engineering debug payloads
Default time window set to last 24 hours with quick presets (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d)
Color palette will reuse Console cost tokens (cost-high, cost-mid, cost-low) and a neutral gray for sampled rows to emphasize uncertainty
